question.problem: If $\log_2(3)=k$ and $\log_2(x)=p,$ what is the value of $\log_2(3x)?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the product rule for logarithms:

$$
\log_n a + \log_n b = \log_n(ab)
$$

Using the product rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{2}⁡(3x) & ={log}_{2}⁡3+{log}_{2}⁡x \\  & =k+p.\end{aligned}
$$
